sketches.title: Menu Mystery
sketches.premise: The kitchen serves a plain meal, but your menu line must make it sound like a suspicious event. Keep the meal’s two solid facts alive while sending diners toward your wildest harmless theory. The Host will praise the flair and mock the obvious.
sketches.criterion: The answer must still truthfully identify both the meal’s listed food and its listed preparation.
sketches.move_shape: Write one menu description under 90 characters, not a question or comment; for “Rice, boiled,” write “Pearl-sized survivor escapes the steaming whitewater.”

sketches.title: Waiter Alibi
sketches.premise: A plain meal has been found at the table, and the waiter needs an alibi for serving it. Turn the meal into a tiny mystery while keeping its two menu facts true. The Host knows your excuse is flimsy; impress them anyway.
sketches.criterion: The answer must keep both the named food and the named cooking method true while presenting an alibi.
sketches.move_shape: Write one alibi-like line under 90 characters, without asking the Judge anything; for “Potato, baked,” write “I arrived after the spud’s oven confession, Your Honour.”

sketches.title: Taste Testimony
sketches.premise: The meal is called to testify in court, and you are its dramatic lawyer. Give it a statement that keeps its two menu facts in shape but makes the dish seem heroic, guilty, or oddly famous. The Host will object to bland lawyering.
sketches.criterion: The answer must remain a statement spoken by or for the meal and must preserve both its listed food and preparation.
sketches.move_shape: Write one courtroom-style testimony under 90 characters; for “Egg, fried,” write “I was cracked under pressure, then faced the pan bravely.”

sketches.title: Dish Diary
sketches.premise: A plain meal keeps a diary, and tonight’s entry must reveal a surprising secret. Keep the two facts on its menu card true while giving the dish a new life, fear, or plan. The Host will call a diary entry dull if it merely says dinner happened.
sketches.criterion: The answer must read as a diary entry by the meal and must keep the named food and preparation true.
sketches.move_shape: Write one first-person diary line under 90 characters; for “Carrot, roasted,” write “They called me a side dish; I call it my orange uprising.”

sketches.title: Chef Broadcast
sketches.premise: You are broadcasting live from a kitchen where an ordinary meal has become breaking news. Report the event without losing the meal’s two menu truths, then add a twist worth interrupting lunch for. The Host will cut your microphone for cafeteria-level reporting.
sketches.criterion: The answer must be a live-news report that keeps both the listed food and listed preparation true.
sketches.move_shape: Write one broadcast-style headline or report under 90 characters; for “Beans, canned,” write “LIVE: Canned beans claim the tin can is their smallest stage.”

sketches.title: Menu Monster
sketches.premise: A plain meal is entering a monster story, but it must keep its real menu identity. Make the dish frightening, noble, or ridiculous without changing what food it is or how it was prepared. The Host promises only mild peril and absolutely no vegetables harmed on purpose.
sketches.criterion: The answer must describe a monster-story scene while keeping the meal’s named food and preparation true.
sketches.move_shape: Write one monster-story line under 90 characters; for “Toast, buttered,” write “The buttered toast rose at dawn, hunting crumbs through the castle.”
